triggers: mlx fast::scaled_dot_product_attention output looks like attention is a no-op or overflows to -inf

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap in mlx fast::scaled_dot_product_attention: the axis contract

problem.statement: mlx fast::scaled_dot_product_attention silently computes attention over the wrong axis

payload.attempted: Feeding (B, seq, heads, dim) shaped q/k/v - the natural reading of diffusion-transformer code and of several mlx examples.
payload.lesson: mlx fast::scaled_dot_product_attention expects (B, heads, seq, dim), torch-style. Verify once with an fp32 softmax reference on a tiny shape; a wrong axis order yields either a trivial no-op attention (seq on the heads axis) or -inf overflows, both silently.

established_fact.mechanism: sdpa reduces over the axis sized seq placed at index 2; with (B,seq,H,D) input the reduction runs over H and the attention degenerates per-token.

payload.observed: (B,S,H,D) input: 2.27 max error vs fp32 softmax reference; (B,H,S,D) input: 0.0012 (fp16 noise).
payload.root_cause: Axis contract undocumented in the C++ header; python docstring examples imply seq-first.

raw.seed: onyx-infer kernel-agent episode E13, stage-verified vs fp32 references on Apple M5 Max, 2026-11-18
